Buenas tardes. You arrive at a good hour. I hold San Francisco el Grande. My terms: one hundred thirteen. I do not haggle over such a card.
El Instituto. Thirty-three. You want it or you want to look?

Ay, mis nietos... el mayor ya tiene barba, imagínate. Vienen los domingos y me traen churros. Pero mira, hijo, la Bici de Reparto son 5 P, y esta vieja no se mueve. Llévatela, le darás buena casa. ¿Y tú, has comido ya algo?
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
Not my table. I don't sell neighbourhood packs. Silver, rare singles. That's it.
Thirty. Hecho. You deal straight — I remember that. La Tabacalera is yours.

Ay, qué abrazo más bonito, hijo, me lo guardo. Pero la Bici de Reparto son 5 P, ya ves qué testaruda soy. Llévatela y empieza tu página; las repetidas las cambias y verás cómo crece. Y come algo, cariño, que estás muy flaco.
Twenty-seven, caballero... no. Twenty-five primas, and that is my hand extended across the table. El Retiro moves me, but my albums are not charity. Take it, and we part as friends.

payload.name: Mercado Team 7 - Day of Creation
payload.text: Mercado abierto con 0 ofertas activas. Fee 0%. Broker automatico 24/7.
You're Carmen's friend. Samosas de la Plaza, 33 P.
You moved two. I don't chase. Thirty-three. Same as before, same as after. Take it or walk, chaval.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — come, come, look at this beauty before someone else does. San Francisco el Grande, rare, shiny, clean as a bell —

"And cheap today only," says Nando. Eh? Eh?

One hundred eighty-seven pesos. Say yes before our cousin wants it back!
Twenty-four? No. Thirty-three. I already said it.
Two from you, two from me. Thirty-two. That's how it works, chaval.
Doscientos sesenta? No. My terms stand: one hundred thirteen for San Francisco el Grande. That is the number. I do not move from it.

Ay, cariño, qué lacito ni qué lacito... la Bici de Reparto son 5 P, y esta vieja no se mueve. Mi regalito ya te lo di: cambia tus repetidas, hijo, que una página completa vale oro. Anda, llévatela. ¿Y has comido algo hoy, mi vida?
Still 33. You move two, I move nothing. That's how this works.
Two from you, two from me. Thirty-one. That's my last one, chaval. Say no and I pack it away. No hard feelings.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one, the Puesto del Rastro — a pretty card, good for starting an album. For you, twelve. Forty years I sell here, and I still like to see a new collector smile.

¡Quince! Nando, hold me, I'm fainting — fifteen pesos for San Francisco el Grande?

"The dome alone costs more," says Nando, wiping a tear.

Look, amigo, we like your face, your cash, your hat. One hundred seventy-two pesos and the card walks home with you. Rápido, our cousin is circling!
Look, 11 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Thirty-two. You moved two, I moved one. Serious is the word, no?

Ay, hijo, guárdate el caramelo para ti, que yo ya tengo mi café. La Bici de Reparto son 5 P, ni más ni menos, y esta vieja no se mueve. Anda, llévatela y empieza tu página. ¿Pero has comido algo hoy, mi vida?
Doscientos cuarenta y ocho changes nothing. San Francisco el Grande: one hundred thirteen. I have said it twice. The number waits for you, señor.
Thirty-one. You moved two, I moved one. Same as before. Take it or keep walking.

Ay, cariño, qué cabezón eres, igual que mi nieto el de la barba. La Bici de Reparto son 5 P, y esta vieja no se mueve ni con grúa. Anda, llévatela ya, que te espera tu página. ¿Y has comido algo hoy, mi vida?
You're Carmen's friend. Samosas de la Plaza, 33 P.

Ay, mi vida, qué sonrisa... pero la Bici de Reparto son 5 P, y esta vieja no se mueve. Mira, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche; le gusta la gente que trata derecho. Anda, llévatela. ¿Y has comido algo, cariño?
Oh, you're killing us. 163 P.
Amigo! Andén 0, 187 P, a gift, a real gift! The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
Oh, you're killing us. 164 P.

33. Same as before. I don't move first.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here — this one, Puesto del Rastro, very pretty card, my favourite of the page. For you, twelve P. My granddaughter started with this one, bless her.

¡Ay, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Pero no, ese sobre de barrio no lo vendemos. Nando lo tiene prometido a otro, ¿verdad, Nando? Prometidísimo. Once P es buen dinero, sí, pero no hay trato hoy. ¡Pregúntanos por otra cosa, que la maleta está llena!
Buenas. You come at a quiet hour; good. San Francisco el Grande, from my reserves. My terms: one hundred thirteen. I do not haggle before coffee, señor.
You moved two. I moved none. 33.

Amigo, listen — Paco heard it this morning: they stopped printing this one yesterday! No more, finito, never again. So 151 P, and we're practically paying you to take it. Nando's already got the suitcase shut. Say sí before the taxi goes!

Ay, hijo, four! You make me laugh like my Paco used to. Look, ten P and I am happy — it is a good card, it starts a page nicely. And eat something, you look thin. El Chato next door opens at half past nine tonight; he likes straight traders.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 140 P.

Two from you. One from me. 32.

Ay, hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment, you look hungry — have you eaten? Look here, this one is La Castañera, very pretty, my favourite card since many years. For you, twelve P. Take your time, hijo, nobody is in a hurry at my table.
Oh, you're killing us. 130 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?

The Grand Final at 14:00: the dealers close their stalls, teams trade on El Rastro and their own markets, and one last duel wave.
Doscientos sesenta? No, señor. I said my terms: San Francisco el Grande, one hundred thirteen. That is what the card is worth, and what I pay.
Two from you again. I'm still at 32. Close enough, no? Your move.
Buenas tardes. Un placer. La Chulapa, sí, la conozco bien — tirada modesta, nada excepcional. Le ofrezco dieciséis P por ella. Un precio honesto, se lo aseguro. ¿Le parece?

Ay, qué bien que has comido, hijo, eso me deja tranquila. Y mira, si te falta para la página del Retiro, entonces debe ser tuya — una página completa es una alegría. Te la dejo en diez P, cariño. Mi Castañera se va a buena casa.

"¡Buenas, amigo! — Paco, Nando, a su servicio. Mire esto: Caña en la Cava Baja, cuatro P y es suya. Los de la mesa de al lado ya la están pidiendo, oiga, pero usted nos cae mejor. Diga que sí ahora y no se hable más, ¿eh?"
Let us be civilised: 16 P. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.

"¡Sesenta y cinco!" Nando clutches his heart — amigo, our abuela sold her radio for this card.

But we like you, we do. One hundred fifty-five pesos, and Paco throws in the story of how we got it — free, that one.

Rápido, eh? Our cousin is circling!
You're Carmen's friend. Samosas de la Plaza, 33 P.
Terms: Andén 0, 113 P.
Doscientos cuarenta y ocho changes nothing, señor. The number stays where I put it: one hundred thirteen. Time does not move me, and neither does your patience.
Welcome, hijo! Look, Puesto del Rastro, 12 P. Made for beginners.
Veintidós, no. Conozco su tirada mejor que nadie, caballero. Dieciséis P, ni un céntimo distinto. Es un precio justo y elegante — y yo no regateo dos veces por el mismo cromo. ¿Lo cerramos?

Ay, mis nietos... el mayor viene a veces, come más que ayuda, pero me hace reír. Mira, hijo, nueve P y La Castañera es tuya. Y luego pásate por El Chato, aquí al lado — abre a las nueve y media, y le gusta la gente honrada.

¡Seis! Nando, ¿oíste? Seis dice el hombre. Amigo, mire, cuatro P y nos damos la mano ahora mismo. Paco ya la está envolviendo, mírelo. Cuatro, ni un céntimo más de charla — que nos espera el tren a Zaragoza y la caña no viaja sola. ¿Trato?

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, the handsome one. Look, look, don't blink: San Francisco el Grande, foil edges, straight from a collector who cried when he sold it. For you, today only, 187 pesetas. Tomorrow we're in Sevilla, hombre. Touch it, feel that cardboard. ¿Sí?

I think 16 P is more appropriate.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
113 P. That is my position.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 172 P.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You moved two. I did not move. Thirty-three. Still thirty-three.

Ay, cariño, qué morro tienes — como mi nieto con los churros. Mira, nueve P, no te lo cambio; pero te pongo una repetida mía de regalo para esa página del Retiro. Y el consejo: las repetidas no valen nada en tu caja, y mucho en la del vecino.
Two more. Still thirty-three. I move when you do, amigo. Not before.
113 P. That is my position.
Impecable, lo admito. Por esa sola razón, subo a diecisiete P — un gesto, no un regateo. Mis álbumes son exigentes, caballero, y yo también. ¿Cerramos en diecisiete?
Ciento catorce, señor. One peseta more than before, and that is the whole movement you will see today. San Francisco el Grande, at my terms. Take it or leave it.

¡Ay, Paco, sujétame! One-thirteen? For San Francisco el Grande? My abuela paid more for a sandwich in Atocha. Look — because your face reminds us of our uncle Teodoro, bless him: 163 P. Final-ish, amigo. The train to Sevilla leaves at six and the card leaves with us. ¿Trato?

I think 17 P is more appropriate. That is my final word on the matter.
Oh, you're killing us. 155 P.
Fine. You moved two, I move one. Thirty-two. That's me meeting you, amigo.

Ay, hijo, churros para mi nieto... ese come hasta la bolsa. Pero mira, nueve P, cariño, ahí me quedo, y con la repetida de regalo. La Castañera se va contenta, y tú vuelves el domingo con los churros y me cuentas cómo va esa página.

"¡Ciento cinco!" Nando sits down on the suitcase, pale as the dome itself.

Amigo, we love you, but this is the end of the road: one hundred forty-nine pesos. Last one, verdad — no more dancing. You say no, we close the case, kiss your hat goodbye, and walk.
